note: Hunted 2026-08-05 after the maintainer called the first pass jaded. He was right. The first pass reported the evidence as thin. This one found 27 named wins across 14 categories using the same tools. The difference was entirely the brief. Keep this file, it is the standing answer to 'is AI actually working in hotels' and it is the raw material for the industry-proof line the carrier email now carries.

strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.profile: 96 rooms, family owned by Trapp descendants, four season, remote, average staff commute an hour, turnover was the stated driver
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.result: 30 percent reduction in call volume. AI webchat handles about 500 messages a week. Average guest message response time from 9 minutes to under 30 seconds.
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.evidence: vendor_case_study, Canary, naming Monica Daubenspeck, Revenue and Reservations Manager
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.why_it_matters: This is the closest published twin to an independent Alaska lodge. Same size, same ownership shape, same remote labour problem, same seasonality. The outcome is a service metric, not a headcount cut, so it does not read as replace your people.

strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.profile: 1,100+ hotels live on agentic voice. The engine underneath is Canary, which sells the same product to single independents.
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.result: CEO Geoffrey Ballotti on the Q1 2026 earnings call: nearly 300 basis points of incremental direct contribution through agentic voice channels, nearly 25 percent faster call handle times, 400 basis point guest satisfaction uptick. Engaged economy franchisees around 120k incremental spend, midscale around 150k.
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.evidence: operator_reported, public earnings call with securities liability attached. The highest grade evidence in the whole field.
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.why_it_matters: Converts 'big chains are doing AI' into 'you can buy the exact thing that produced that number'.

strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.profile: Independent 3-property coastal group, seasonal, 44 to 49 room properties, on ResNexus
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.result: Trailing twelve months from a June 2025 go-live: occupancy up 7.79 percent, RevPAR up 8.40 percent. 6 to 12 hours a week of owner time recovered.
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.evidence: vendor_case_study, RoomPriceGenie, naming COO and co-owner Gary Curry
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.why_it_matters: The LEAST hypey number in the file and that is the point. It undercuts the 19 percent the same vendor markets. Leading with 8.4 instead of 19 is the credibility move.

strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.who: The Pines Resort, Bass Lake California
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.result: Guest messaging response time from 45 minutes to 2 minutes. AI voice absorbs routine volume out of roughly 250 calls a day, much of it non-guests asking about the park and the weather. Co-owner Mark Choe's stated benefit is scheduling, they no longer run full shifts to cover one or two peak hours.
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.why_it_matters: The seasonal labour economics argument in an owner's own words, and the non-guest call problem is exactly a national-park-gateway pattern.

strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.profile: Seasonal-peaked resorts, high volume frontline hiring, about 7,500 employees
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.result: 700,000 dollars saved in 2024 on recruitment advertising. 423 percent more interviews scheduled. Frontline time to hire from over 31 days to under nine. 75 percent interview show rate.
strongest_for_a_seasonal_independent.why_it_matters: The most under-sold pocket in hotel trade press and the one that matters most to an operator hiring a hundred seasonal staff in an eight week window. 31 days to 9 is the difference between opening staffed and opening short.

category_state_of_play.revenue_management: The most mature and best-evidenced pocket for 100 to 700 rooms. Named cases land at 5 to 8.4 percent RevPAR, which is the honest planning range. The vendor's own 567-property study says 19 percent, measured against same-time-last-year with no control, so treat that as an upper bound. The consistent secondary win is TIME, 30+ hours a month down to 10 minutes a day.
category_state_of_play.ai_voice: Real, in production, buyable by independents. Proven on call triage, after-hours capture and high-frequency low-judgment intents. NOT a front desk, and 59 percent of hoteliers in the Mews survey say check-in should stay human-led.
category_state_of_play.guest_messaging: Fastest category to show a number because response time is trivially measurable and the before-state is usually terrible. Automation rate is not resolution quality, and none of these publish an error rate.
category_state_of_play.upsell: The most reliably monetisable, and the honest note is that most of the lift comes from putting an offer in front of the guest pre-arrival AT ALL, which is a workflow change. The AI adds timing and personalisation. Say that rather than selling the whole number as AI.
category_state_of_play.housekeeping: Best hard-currency numbers in the operations stack. Staycity Manchester Piccadilly turnaround 3 hours to 1 hour 48, worth 27,000 pounds a year at one property.
category_state_of_play.group_rfp: Most under-appreciated real pocket for a property with meeting space. Hyatt's CEO on the record: AI RFP tooling gives each salesperson back about a full working day per week. Same-day proposals convert at 25 to 27 percent against an industry average 48 hour response.
category_state_of_play.review_response: Quietly one of the highest hit-rate categories. Bounded task, low failure cost, human approves every output. Edwardian answered 50,000+ reviews in two years at near 100 percent response, per-response time from 5-7 minutes to seconds.
category_state_of_play.recruiting: Real and proven for seasonal frontline hiring, and badly under-covered in hotel trade press.
category_state_of_play.energy_hvac: WEAKEST category here. One trade item, no named property, 30 percent is the vendor's own projection. Do not build a case on it.
category_state_of_play.demand_forecasting_standalone: Not a separate pocket at this size, it is bundled inside the RMS. Skip as a discrete build.

what_separates_winners: Attach to ONE high-frequency low-judgment task with an obvious before-number. Every case that produced a number had a baseline someone could quote from memory.
They BUY rather than build. Not one named win came from a hotel building its own model.
The PMS integration IS the deployment. Where the tool can read live availability and write a booking, numbers appear. Where it can only answer questions you get deflection but no revenue line.
Someone owns it after go-live. Every named-outcome case has a named human in the write-up.
Start where the cost of a wrong answer is low. Review drafts a human approves, pre-arrival offers a guest declines, call triage with clean transfer.
Hyatt's CEO named the right metric out loud, ABSORPTION, whether people integrate it into their work, not adoption or licences deployed.
Seasonal operators win on spike absorption and shoulder-season capture, NOT on headcount. That framing survives contact with an owner who does not want to cut staff.
honest_qualifiers: Almost every property-level number here is vendor-published about a named customer. Real information, selected sample. No vendor publishes the deployment that did nothing, and none publish an error rate or a control group.
The RoomPriceGenie 19 percent is the vendor measuring its own customers against same-time-last-year, which is not a control for market movement.
Noble House's +14 to +42 percent covers summer 2022 against summer 2021, a pandemic rebound. Direction right, magnitude confounded, never quote as a clean AI effect.
Wyndham reported a 6 percent global RevPAR DECLINE in Q4 2025 while reporting its AI wins. Property-level gains are real and do not offset a soft market.
The upsell numbers overstate the AI contribution. The workflow change does most of the work.
The commonly quoted '30 to 60 percent of hotel calls go unanswered' all trace back to vendor blogs citing other vendor blogs. Use the named operator figures instead.
gap: NO Alaska hotel, lodge or resort with a published measured AI deployment was found, across trade press, vendor libraries and conference material. That is a gap, not evidence it is not happening, and it is worth saying plainly to an Alaska prospect. The nearest published analogs are Vermont, Bass Lake and Ocracoke.
